title: Chapter 7 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of scaling, probes, and resource management.

questions.question: What does a CPU request of 250m mean?
options: The container will use exactly 0.25 cores
The container is guaranteed 250 millicores (0.25 core) for scheduling
The container cannot use more than 250 millicores
The container will be throttled to 25% CPU
questions.explanation: Requests are used for scheduling and guarantee a minimum amount of CPU.

questions.question: What happens when a container exceeds its memory limit?
options: It is migrated to another node
It continues running but with warnings
questions.explanation: Memory is incompressible; exceeding the limit triggers an OOM kill.

questions.question: Which QoS class does a Pod get if all containers have equal requests and limits for CPU and memory?
questions.explanation: Guaranteed QoS requires equal requests and limits for all containers.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a readiness probe?
options: To check if a container is ready to serve traffic
To check if a container is alive and restart if not
To initialise the container with data
questions.explanation: Readiness probes determine if the Pod should receive traffic.

questions.question: What happens when a readiness probe fails?
options: The Pod is removed from Service endpoints
questions.explanation: Failing readiness stops traffic but doesn't restart the container.

questions.question: The three types of probe handlers are httpGet, tcpSocket, and _____.
questions.explanation: exec runs a command inside the container.

questions.question: What is the main difference between liveness and readiness probes?
options: Liveness restarts the container on failure, readiness stops traffic
Readiness restarts the container, liveness stops traffic
Both do the same thing but have different names
Liveness is for HTTP, readiness is for TCP
questions.explanation: Liveness leads to container restart; readiness affects service routing.

questions.question: What should you avoid checking in a liveness probe?
questions.explanation: Checking external dependencies can cause cascading restarts.

questions.question: When should you use a startup probe?
options: For containers that need frequent restarts
For containers with a long initial startup time
For containers that never become ready
For containers without any other probes
questions.explanation: Startup probes delay liveness/readiness until the app is fully initialised.

questions.question: True or False: A startup probe runs periodically even after initial success.
questions.explanation: Once it succeeds once, it never runs again.

questions.question: What component does the HPA rely on for CPU/memory metrics by default?
questions.explanation: The Metrics Server provides resource metrics for HPA.

questions.question: Which command creates an HPA for a Deployment targeting 50% CPU?
questions.explanation: `kubectl autoscale` is the imperative command.

questions.question: Why must Pods have CPU requests for HPA to work?
options: HPA calculates utilisation as a percentage of requests
CPU limits are mandatory for HPA
questions.explanation: Without requests, utilisation percentage cannot be computed.

questions.question: If an HPA defines both CPU (target 50%) and memory (target 80%), how does it determine replicas?
options: It takes the average of both
It picks the metric yielding the highest replica count
questions.explanation: The max of all metric calculations is used.

questions.question: What is the stabilisation window in HPA?
options: The time to wait before scaling up
The time to wait before scaling down
Both up and down windows to prevent flapping
questions.explanation: Stabilisation windows (scaleUp and scaleDown) prevent rapid fluctuations.

questions.question: True or False: HPA can scale on custom metrics like requests per second.
questions.explanation: HPA supports custom and external metrics via adapters.

questions.question: Which probe would you use to prevent a Pod from receiving traffic while its cache warms up?
questions.explanation: Readiness controls traffic; use it to delay service inclusion.

questions.question: What happens if a startup probe never succeeds within `failureThreshold * periodSeconds`?
options: The container continues running but never gets traffic
questions.explanation: Exceeding the startup probe's failure threshold causes a container restart.

questions.question: To check current CPU/memory usage of Pods, use the command `kubectl top _____`.
questions.explanation: `kubectl top pods` shows resource usage.

questions.question: Which QoS class has the lowest priority during node memory pressure?
questions.explanation: BestEffort Pods are evicted first because they have no resource guarantees.
